question.q: Which food element most reliably softens the perception of tannin?
question.exp: Tannin binds with protein, which is why a rare steak makes a young tannic red seem rounder. Fat coats the palate and blunts the same astringency.

question.q: A dish high in acidity demands what of the wine, if the wine is not to taste flat?
question.exp: Acid in the dish resets the palate and makes a lower-acid wine taste dull and flabby. Meeting it keeps the wine tasting fresh.

findings.claim: The grader refuses plainly right answers such as 'increases them', 'increases', 'accentuates both', 'heightens them' and 'makes them harsher'.
findings.because: The accept entries are two-word phrases ('increases both', 'accentuates them'). A one-word input like 'increases' fails the 60% word-coverage rule (it needs 2 words). 'Increases them' and 'accentuates both' are not substrings of any entry, and no entry is contained in them. The negation guard in matchSA already handles 'does not increase', so single-word accepts are safe here.
findings.fix: accept: ["increases both", "makes them more prominent", "accentuates them", "increases", "increase", "accentuates", "heightens", "emphasizes", "amplifies", "harsher", "more bitter"]
findings.verifyReason:
I confirmed the finding by running the real matchSA from js/core.js in node against the current accept list. The grader refuses plainly right answers: "increases", "increases them", "accentuates both", "heightens them", "heightens both", "amplifies them", "emphasizes them", "makes them harsher", "makes them more pronounced", "harder and more bitter" and "it increases them" are all graded false. The keyed answer itself is correct: cold hardens tannin and sharpens bitterness, which is standard serving-temperature doctrine.

The proposed fix is off, though, because its single-word entries open holes that it says the negation guard closes. The guard does not catch "doesn't": norm turns it into "doesn t", and neither NEG_RE nor NEG_PHRASES contains "doesn" (only "dont" and "don t"). With the examiner's list, "doesn't increase them" grades CORRECT through the bare "increase" entry. The same list also passes "increases fruitiness" and "decreases tannin, increases fruit". A bare "more pronounced" would also pass "more pronounced aroma".

The replacement below keeps the entries to verb + both/them pairs and full phrases, plus the plural-only bare "increases". I tested it in node:
- Every right phrasing above grades true.
- "doesn't increase them", "does not increase them", "softens them", "reduces both", "less prominent", "makes them less pronounced" and "more pronounced aroma" all grade false.
- The only residual leak is the bare "increases" (it passes "increases fruitiness"). I accept that trade because a one-word "increases" is a plainly right answer to this stem.

Outside this finding: the "doesn't"/"doesn t" gap in NEG_RE is a grader-wide flaw in core.js and deserves its own fix.

question.q: Serving a red too cold does what to its tannin and bitterness?
question.exp: Cold hardens tannin and sharpens bitterness while muting aroma. An over-chilled red often reads as a bad pairing when it is only a service fault.
